cities.base: Nørrebro or Vesterbro, where the city actually lives: bakeries, wine bars and the lakes on foot, ten minutes by bike to everything, and a third cheaper than Indre By. Roskilde, Helsingør and Møn all w
cities.name: Copenhagen

cities.base: Frederiksbjerg, south of the station around Jægergårdsgade: the best bars and bistros are on your street, the Latin Quarter is a fifteen minute walk, and the Marselisborg forest and the beach are twen
cities.name: Aarhus

cities.base: The old quarter between Overgade and Vestergade, five minutes from the station and next to the Andersen museum. One night on the way between Copenhagen and Aarhus is the right dose; two only if Egesko
cities.name: Odense

cities.base: Vesterby, the yellow streets between the station and the harbour; Gammel Skagen 4 km west is prettier and quieter but you need a bike for dinner. Five hours from Copenhagen by train with two changes,
cities.name: Skagen

cities.base: Gudhjem or Svaneke on the east coast, not Rønne where the ferry lands: the smokehouses, the round churches and the coast path are all within a bus ride, and both harbours are worth an evening. Hire bi
cities.name: Bornholm

cities.base: No beds at the cliff. A long day from Copenhagen: train to Vordingborg, bus 660R to Stege, bus 678 to the GeoCenter, about 2 hours 20 each way in season. With a hire car it is 1 hour 45.
cities.name: Møns Klint

cities.base: Day trip on the Kystbanen coast train, 46 minutes from Copenhagen H, three trains an hour; Kronborg is a ten minute walk from the station. Pair it with Louisiana, which is two stops back down the same
cities.name: Helsingør

places.name: Restaurant Schønnemann
places.note: Smørrebrød since 1877 in a cellar off Hauser Plads: lunch only, book a week ahead, order two pieces and a snaps and stop there; the herring and the smoked eel with scrambled egg are the point.

places.name: Selma
places.note: The modern smørrebrød place, a Swedish chef doing the classics with better bread and a Michelin nod; lunch is the thing, dinner is Wednesday to Saturday only, and it is shut all day Tuesday.

places.name: noma
places.note: Reopened 5 August 2026 after Redzepi stepped back, with a new monthly menu at 4,500 DKK before wine, Wednesday to Saturday only, and it lost its stars in the 2026 guide; still the most ambitious kitchen in the country, no longer the sure thing, and booked out months ahead.

places.name: Hart Bageri
places.note: The Tartine alumnus's bakery on Gammel Kongevej and the best morning bun in a city of them; the cardamom croissant sells out by ten, and there is a second branch on Refshaleøen.

places.name: Hija de Sanchez, Kødbyen
places.note: Rosio Sanchez, ex-noma pastry chef, nixtamalising her own corn in the old meatpacking district; three tacos and a michelada is lunch, and the Torvehallerne stand is the same food with a queue.

places.name: Bæst
places.note: Christian Puglisi's pizzeria with its own mozzarella dairy upstairs and charcuterie from its own farm; the pizza is the best in the city and the salumi board is why you book, every night of the week.

places.name: SMK, the National Gallery
places.note: Free for the permanent collection, which is the Danish Golden Age, Hammershøi and a Matisse room; shut Mondays, open until 20:00 on Wednesdays, and the special shows cost 130 to 175 DKK.

places.name: Church of Our Saviour spire
places.note: 400 steps, the last 150 outside on a spiral that narrows to nothing, for the best view in the city; book a slot, go before eleven, and it shuts the moment it rains or blows, and all of January.

places.name: Tivoli at dusk
places.note: 165 to 195 DKK just to walk in, rides extra, and it is worth it exactly once, after dark when the lamps come on; runs April to September, then two weeks of Halloween and the Christmas season from mid-November, shut in between.

places.name: The Little Mermaid
places.note: A small bronze on a rock, ringed by coaches from eight in the morning; if you must, see it on the walk round the Kastellet ramparts and keep going, do not make it the destination.

places.name: Copenhagen Contemporary
places.note: Large-scale installation art in an old welding hall, three or four shows at a time; shut Mondays, open to 21:00 Thursdays, and it sits next to Lille Bakery and the harbour sauna so make an afternoon of the island.

places.name: Superkilen and Jægersborggade
places.note: BIG's red and black park with street furniture from sixty countries, then Jægersborggade's ceramics shops, coffee and a wine bar or two; this is the Nørrebro people mean when they say stay in Nørrebro.

places.name: Ved Stranden 10
places.note: The wine bar on the canal opposite Christiansborg, natural and classical both, small plates and a room that feels like a friend's flat; a glass costs what a bottle does at home, and it is shut Sundays.

places.name: Lille Bakery
places.note: Sourdough, morning buns and a proper lunch plate in a shed on the old shipyard, with the sauna and Copenhagen Contemporary next door; shut Monday and Tuesday, so plan the island day around it.

places.name: Viking Ship Museum, Roskilde
places.note: Twenty-five minutes on the train: five longships raised from the fjord in 1962 and a boatyard building new ones by hand; 165 DKK in summer, 130 in winter, and the cathedral with forty royal tombs is a 12 minute walk up the hill.

places.name: ARoS
places.note: Eliasson's rainbow walkway on the roof and Ron Mueck's five metre Boy in the basement, with a serious Danish collection between; 200 DKK, shut Mondays, open to 20:00 on weeknights in winter, and the roof is best an hour before sunset.

places.name: Den Gamle By
places.note: Seventy-five real buildings moved here from all over Denmark and staffed in costume, from 1600s merchant houses to a 1974 street with a working record shop; open daily, about 215 DKK in season, cheaper before 28 March, and the 1970s block is the part adults remember.

places.name: Moesgaard Museum
places.note: Grauballe Man, the bog body, in the best archaeology building in Europe, a grass wedge you walk up the roof of; bus 18 takes 25 minutes from the centre, it is shut Mondays and open to 21:00 Wednesdays, and the forest trail down to the beach afterwards is 3 km.

places.name: The Latin Quarter and the cathedral
places.note: The oldest streets, Volden, Graven and Klostergade, are two hundred metres of small shops, cafes and one good coffee roaster, with the longest church in Denmark at the bottom; an hour, no more, and it is quiet on a Sunday.

places.name: La Cabra
places.note: The roaster that put Aarhus on the coffee map, now in New York and Bangkok too; the Graven cafe does its own pastries, and the cardamom bun is the equal of anything in Copenhagen.

places.name: Aarhus Street Food
places.note: Thirty stalls in an old bus garage behind the station, from bao to Danish hot dogs, all around 100 DKK a plate; fine rather than thrilling, but it is the cheap dinner in a city short of them and it runs every night.

places.name: Frederikshøj
places.note: Wassim Hallal's restaurant in the Marselisborg woods, two Michelin stars in 2026 and the best table in Jutland; Thursday to Saturday only from 17:30, twenty or so servings, and you need to book weeks out and take a taxi back.

places.name: Hærværk
places.note: Whole animals, vegetables from named farms and natural wine, no choices on the menu and a Michelin green star; the honest version of new Nordic at a third of the price, and it is shut Sunday and Monday.

places.name: Pondus
places.note: The bistro run by the Substans team on the canal, a Bib Gourmand and a three course set menu around 350 DKK that changes weekly; the sensible dinner in Aarhus, book a day ahead, closed Sunday and Monday.

places.name: St. Pauls Apothek and Jægergårdsgade
places.note: An old pharmacy turned cocktail bar on the street where Aarhus goes out; start here, then work up Jægergårdsgade through Mikkeller and the pizza place, and you will not need a plan.

places.name: Reduktivt
places.note: A natural wine bar and bottle shop on Borggade with a dozen things by the glass and cheese and bread to go with them; small, unbothered by tourists, and shut Sundays.

places.name: Aarhus Ø harbour bath and the Salling roof
places.note: The new docklands: BIG's free harbour bath with a 50 m pool and a diving tower, open June to September, the Iceberg apartment block, and back in the centre the Salling department store roof with a glass ledge you stand on for free.

places.name: Marselisborg forest, the deer park and the Infinite Bridge
places.note: Forty minutes on foot south along the water: the royal palace gardens, a free deer park where the sika eat from your hand, and at Varna beach the circular wooden pier that stands in the sea from April to October and is taken down for winter.

places.name: H.C. Andersens Hus
places.note: Kengo Kuma's 2021 museum sunk into a garden around the house where Andersen was born, and far better than the name suggests; timed entry, 195 DKK, daily in summer but closed Mondays November to March, and the childhood home ticket is included for 30 days.

places.name: Andersen's childhood home
places.note: Two rooms on Munkemøllestræde where the family lived until he left for Copenhagen at 14; ten minutes, included with the main museum, shut Mondays.

places.name: Brandts
places.note: The art museum in an old cloth mill, Danish painting upstairs and photography and contemporary shows below, with the best courtyard cafes in town around it; shut Mondays, open to 21:00 Thursdays.

places.name: Den Fynske Landsby
places.note: An open-air village of thatched Funen farms with animals and a working smithy, 25 minutes up the river path from the centre or bus 110; open April to October and Christmas weekends, shut Mondays outside July, and quiet in a way Den Gamle By is not.

places.name: Storms Pakhus
places.note: Street food and bars in a harbour warehouse, twenty kitchens and a courtyard; the cheap dinner in Odense, loud on Fridays, and a ten minute walk north from the station.

places.name: Sortebro Kro
places.note: A 1805 coaching inn at the gate of Den Fynske Landsby doing classic Danish lunch, herring, fried plaice and the Funen rye; pair it with the village, and check the day, it is shut Sunday evening and Monday.

places.name: Restaurant Aro
places.note: Odense's Michelin star in a converted machine factory, five or seven courses from their own farm, Wednesday to Saturday from 18:00; less formal than the Copenhagen equivalents and about half the price.

places.name: Nelle's Coffee & Wine
places.note: The Overgade branch of the local cafe chain, on the pedestrian street by the museum; a good flat white and a pastry in the morning, a glass of wine at five, and it is where the town sits.

places.name: Anarkist Beer & Food Lab
places.note: The Albani brewery's experimental taproom with forty of its own beers and a burger kitchen, in the old bottling hall a five minute walk from the centre; the local night out, not a craft-beer shrine.

places.name: Munke Mose and the river path
places.note: The park on the Odense river and the flat path south along it to the Fruens Bøge woods; from May to September the Odense Aafart boat does the same 3 km in 35 minutes for about 90 DKK if the legs have had enough.

places.name: Egeskov Castle
places.note: A 1554 castle standing in a lake, 265 DKK online for the castle, gardens, mazes, treetop walk and the car museum; 25 minutes by train to Kværndrup and 2 km on foot, open daily 28 March to 25 October, shut the rest of the year.

places.name: Grenen
places.note: The sandbar where the Skagerrak and the Kattegat meet and you can stand with a foot in each; 1.5 km on sand from the car park at the end of bus 99 or a 4 km bike ride, the Sandormen tractor for those who will not walk, and no swimming, the current kills.

places.name: Skagens Museum
places.note: Krøyer, Ancher and the painters who came for the light in the 1880s, in the garden of the hotel where they drank; shut Mondays outside July and August, and the ticket also covers Anchers Hus.

places.name: Anchers Hus
places.note: Michael and Anna Ancher's house left exactly as it was, 250 paintings on the walls of the rooms they were painted in; on the museum ticket, and it is closed for winter after 18 October 2026 and reopens 19 March 2027, then Tuesday to Sunday 10:00 to 16:00.

places.name: Den Tilsandede Kirke
places.note: A 14th century church abandoned in 1795 when the sand won; only the tower stands out of the dune now, 4 km south of town on the cycle path, and the interior is open June to August only.

places.name: Råbjerg Mile
places.note: A square kilometre of bare sand 40 m high walking north-east at 15 m a year; 16 km south-west of Skagen, so a bike or the car, and the wind up top will strip paint.

places.name: Skagen Fiskerestaurant
places.note: Sawdust on the floor, fish landed 50 m away and a singer with a guitar every summer night; the shrimp are the order, it is mobbed in July, and it closes for most of the winter.

places.name: Pakhuset
places.note: The old fish warehouse on the quay, fish soup and fried plaice downstairs at lunch and Restaurant Håkon upstairs for a longer dinner; the harbour-side tables are the reason to come.

places.name: Brøndums Hotel
places.note: The dining room where the painters ate on credit, still hung with their portraits of each other; classic Danish dinner, good and not cheap, and worth it once for the room.

places.name: Gammel Skagen sunset
places.note: The west coast village 4 km from town, thatched yellow houses and a dune platform called Solnedgangspladsen where the whole town turns up at dusk; ride out, watch it go down into the Skagerrak, ride back.

places.name: Skagen Grå Fyr
places.note: The 1858 grey lighthouse on the way to Grenen, now a bird migration centre; 95 DKK in season for the exhibition and 210 steps to a view of both seas, 50 DKK for the tower alone in winter.

places.name: Skagen Bryghus
places.note: The town brewery in the old power station, eight of its own beers and a pub kitchen; the one place open late in the off season, and the beer garden fills by six in July.

places.name: Hammershus
places.note: The largest medieval ruin in northern Europe on a cliff 74 m over the sea, free and always open, with a visitor centre and a Kadeau-run cafe from April to October; bus 1 from Rønne or Allinge, and the coast path south from it is the better half of the morning.

places.name: Helligdomsklipperne coast path
places.note: Seven kilometres of granite cliff path from Gudhjem to the Helligdommen rocks and the art museum, up and down the whole way with ladders into a sea cave at the end; bus 3 back, or the boat from Gudhjem in summer.

places.name: Bornholms Kunstmuseum
places.note: Bornholm's painters and a building with a stream running through the floor, on the cliff above Helligdomsklipperne; 100 DKK, shut Mondays April to October and open Friday to Sunday only in winter.

places.name: Østerlars Rundkirke
places.note: The largest of the island's four round churches, a 12th century fortress with a hollow pillar you climb inside; a few kroner in the box, on the road between Gudhjem and Svaneke, and closed to visitors during Sunday services.

places.name: Svaneke Røgeri
places.note: Four generations of alder-smoked herring under the white chimneys on the harbour; order Sol over Gudhjem, a smoked herring with a raw yolk, chives and radish on rye, eat it outside, and go before one; seasonal, most smokehouses are shut in winter.

places.name: Hasle Røgeri
places.note: The last smokehouse on the island still smoking in the old open ovens, a 20 minute bus ride north of the Rønne ferry; the buffet is the deal, and it is a summer place, shut from autumn to Easter.

places.name: Svaneke Bryghus
places.note: The organic brewery on the square in Denmark's prettiest town, with a pub kitchen and a courtyard; the evening in Svaneke, and Bryghuset's beers are in every shop on the island.

places.name: Kadeau Bornholm
places.note: The original Kadeau, a Michelin star since 2016 in a beach house on the south coast, everything pickled, smoked or foraged on the island; a summer place, May to September, closed in winter, Thursday to Sunday plus Wednesdays in high season, taxi from Aakirkeby, and book the day the season opens.

places.name: Dueodde
places.note: Sand so fine it was once sold for hourglasses, dunes, a shallow warm sea and a 47 m lighthouse to climb; bus 7 from Rønne or Nexø, and the only beach in Denmark you would cross a country for.

places.name: The Christiansø boat
places.note: Departs Gudhjem at 10:00, an hour to a 1684 naval fortress on two granite islets joined by a footbridge, back by 15:00 or 16:30, daily in season and a winter mail boat on a timetable to check; around 320 DKK return, cancelled in a strong wind, and there is one cafe out there.

places.name: Gudhjem and Bokul
places.note: The steepest village in Denmark, half-timbered houses stacked above two harbours, and the Bokul rock behind it for the view along the coast at sunset; the ice cream and the smokehouse on the harbour are the evening.

places.name: Restaurant Nordlandet
places.note: The hotel restaurant on the rocks at Allinge, a four course menu of island fish and vegetables at 690 DKK and smørrebrød at lunch; sit by the window, and it is shut for the winter like most of the north coast.

places.name: Maglevandstrappen and the cliff beach
places.note: 497 wooden steps from the GeoCenter down 128 m of chalk to a beach of flint and belemnite fossils, then back up the Store Klint stairs and along the forest top; the climb is the day, and the beach is impassable at high water after a storm.

places.name: GeoCenter Møns Klint
places.note: The visitor centre on the cliff top with 70 million years of chalk and dinosaurs, good for a rainy hour and the only cafe up here; 155 DKK, open 21 March to 30 October, shut for the winter.

places.name: Liselund
places.note: A 1790s romantic park with a thatched miniature palace, Swiss and Chinese follies and paths down to the cliff; free, 3 km north of the GeoCenter along the cliff path, and empty on a weekday.

places.name: Elmelunde Kirke
places.note: A whitewashed village church with the best 15th century frescoes in Denmark across every vault, painted by the Elmelunde Master; on the bus route back to Stege, free, open daytime except during services.

places.name: Stege
places.note: The market town where the buses change, with the only surviving medieval town gate in Denmark and a main street of bakeries and one good fish shop; you will have an hour here whether you want it or not, so use it for lunch.

places.name: Kronborg
places.note: Hamlet's Elsinore, a 1580s fortress guarding the Sound with the casemates and Holger Danske asleep in the basement; 150 DKK, open daily April to October and shut Mondays the rest of the year, and go at ten before the coaches from Copenhagen.

places.name: M/S Museet for Søfart
places.note: BIG's maritime museum built underground around a dry dock next to the castle, and better than the castle for anyone who likes buildings; 135 DKK, shut Mondays outside July and August.

places.name: Helsingør old town and Sankt Olai
places.note: Stengade and Strandgade, the best-kept medieval street grid in Denmark with the cathedral in the middle; an hour between the castle and the train, and quieter than anything in Copenhagen.

places.name: Værftets Madmarked
places.note: Street food hall in the old shipyard between the station and the castle, a dozen kitchens and tables on the quay; the lunch on a castle day, and it is quieter on weekdays.

places.name: The ferry to Helsingborg
places.note: Twenty minutes across the Sound to Sweden and back, the ferries leave every 15 minutes and the Danes ride them for the duty-free; a cheap way to see Kronborg from the water, bring a passport.

places.name: Restaurant HOS
places.note: Modern smørrebrød at lunch, herring at 140 DKK, smoked salmon 160, beef tartare 170, so two pieces is about 300; in late October the evening menu is the game menu. Wednesday to Saturday only, last lunch booking 14:00, reserve ahead.

places.name: Restaurant Oluf Bagers Gaard
places.note: A historic house split into a formal room and a casual one; lunch is three smørrebrød for 215 DKK or the stjerneskud at 225, and dinner is a 9-course sharing menu. Lunch 12:00 to 15:00, dinner from 17:30, closed Sunday, book at weekends.

places.name: Rosenborg Castle
places.note: Christian IV's summer house, begun 1606, with the Crown Jewels and the coronation chair in the Long Hall. 140 DKK online for a timed slot, go at opening; daily to 17:00 until 2 Nov, then 10:00 to 16:00 and closed Mondays.

places.name: National Museum of Denmark
places.note: 14,000 years of Denmark: the Trundholm Sun Chariot, the Egtved Girl's oak coffin and the Gundestrup cauldron; the Golden Horns are copies, the originals were melted in 1802. 130 DKK, under-18s free, closed Mondays November to March.

places.name: Rundetaarn (Round Tower)
places.note: Christian IV's observatory, finished 1642, climbed by a 7.5-turn ramp built so a carriage could reach the library, to a deck 34.8 m up. 60 DKK; October to March to 21:00 on Monday and Tuesday, when the telescope is open if the sky is clear.

places.name: Christiansborg Palace
places.note: Parliament, the PM's office and the Supreme Court over the ruins of Bishop Absalon's 1167 castle. Reception Rooms 150 DKK, Ruins 85, the tower free; 10:00 to 17:00 to 1 Nov, winter hours vary, check, and it can close for state events.

places.name: Kastellet
places.note: The star-shaped citadel, rebuilt 1662 to 1665 for Frederik III and still a working army base; free, walk the ramparts past the 1840s windmill and catch the guard change at 12:00. The Little Mermaid is 600 m on. Gate hours vary, check.

places.name: Ny Carlsberg Glyptotek
places.note: Greek, Roman and Egyptian sculpture and French painting to 1920, around a palm Winter Garden under the dome; about $21, free the last Wednesday of the month, Thursday to 21:00, closed Monday. A big restoration is coming, so check dates.

places.name: Church of Our Lady (Vor Frue Kirke)
places.note: The cathedral C. F. Hansen rebuilt after the British shelled the old one in 1807, consecrated 1829, with Thorvaldsen's marble Christ and Twelve Apostles down the nave. Free, donations welcome; skip 08:05 to 08:25 on weekdays, when a service is broadcast.

places.name: Vippefyret
places.note: The old tilting beacon fire tower by the road out to Grenen, a ten minute stop on the way to the tip rather than a trip of its own; no fee listed, and hours vary, check.

places.name: Kystmuseet Skagen
places.note: The museum of Skagen's fishing and rescue at sea; about $18, Tuesday to Friday from 10:00, weekends from 11:00, to 16:00 and closed Monday. Winter hours are not confirmed, so check before you go.

places.name: Bornholms Museum
places.note: Island history from the Stone Age on: over 1,800 gold-foil guldgubber from Sorte Muld and a room on the Soviet bombing of Rønne and Nexø in May 1945. 100 DKK; winter weekdays 13:00 to 16:00, Saturday 11:00 to 15:00, closed Sunday, check.

places.name: Nylars Round Church
places.note: The oldest of the four round churches, built around 1165, with the only original Romanesque window of the four and a 13th century Creation fresco round the central pillar. Free; hours vary, check.

places.name: Rytterknægten and the Kongemindet tower
places.note: The island's highest point, 162 m, in Almindingen forest, with a granite tower built for Frederik VII's 1851 visit and a steel top from 1899. Free in daylight; the trees now block much of the view, so come for the forest.

places.name: NaturBornholm
places.note: Bornholm's geology and nature indoors and out, 150 DKK; seasonal, 31 Oct 2026 is the last day of the season and it is closed in winter, with no reopening date announced, so it only works on a spring or summer trip.

places.name: Oluf Høst Museum
places.note: The painter Oluf Høst's house and studio in Gudhjem, about $15; open 11:00 to 17:00 daily in season, closed for winter, and it reopens 13 Mar 2027.

outings.why: Chalk cliffs 128 m above the Baltic, 497 steps down to a beach of flint and fossils and a forest loop back along the top; the transport is the hard part, 2 hours 20 each way by train and two buses, and the buses stop at 5 pm.
outings.name: Møns Klint and the Maglevand stairs
outings.season: April to October for the GeoCenter and bus 678; the cliff it
outings.fallback: Liselund park and the top path only, no stairs, 2 hours on site.

outings.why: Hamlet's castle at 10 when it opens, the maritime museum next door, then two stops back to Humlebæk for Louisiana until dark; all on one train line, and the only hard part is not lingering at Kronborg.
outings.name: Kronborg and Louisiana on the Kystbanen
outings.season: All year; Louisiana is shut Mondays and Kronborg is shut Mon
outings.fallback: Louisiana alone, 5 hours door to door.

outings.why: Twenty-five minutes on the train, five real longships raised from the fjord and the boatyard that rebuilds them, then the cathedral with forty kings in it; May to September add an hour rowing a replica on the fjord.
outings.name: Roskilde: the Viking ships and the cathedral
outings.season: All year; boat trips May to September

outings.why: Twenty minutes on the S-train to Klampenborg, then a royal deer park with two thousand deer and a hunting lodge on a hill, and Arne Jacobsen's beach across the road; flat, free and the best half day out of the city.
outings.name: Dyrehaven and a swim at Bellevue
outings.season: All year; swimming June to August
outings.fallback: The beach and the lodge only, 2 hours.

outings.why: Bus 18 to the museum on the hill, Grauballe Man and the grass roof, then the 3 km trail through Moesgaard forest to the beach and the coast path back toward town; the museum is shut Mondays.
outings.name: Moesgaard and the forest down to the beach

outings.why: The best-preserved moated Renaissance castle in Europe, with a maze, a treetop walk and a hall of vintage cars; 25 minutes by train to Kværndrup then a 2 km walk, and the ticket is 265 DKK so give it the whole afternoon.
outings.name: Egeskov
outings.fallback: Den Fynske Landsby, the open-air village in Odense, 2 hours.

outings.why: North 4 km to the tip where the two seas meet and you walk the last kilometre on sand, then south past the buried church to the migrating dune; 35 km of flat cycle path and a headwind one way, guaranteed.
outings.name: Grenen and Råbjerg Mile by bike
outings.season: All year; bike hire and the Sandormen tractor 28 March to 24

outings.why: Bus to the largest castle ruin in northern Europe, free, on a cliff 74 m over the sea, then the coast path south past Opalsøen and the Hammer lighthouse to Allinge for a harbour lunch; rocky underfoot but never steep.
outings.name: Hammershus and the north coast path
outings.season: All year; visitor centre and cafe April to October
outings.fallback: Hammershus and the visitor centre only, 3 hours.

outings.why: An hour by boat from Gudhjem to a 17th century naval fortress on two granite islets with 90 residents and no cars; you get four hours ashore, and the boat does not sail in a stiff easterly.
outings.name: Christiansø on the morning boat
outings.season: Daily 20 April to 18 October, weekdays only in winter
outings.fallback: Gudhjem to Helligdomsklipperne on the coast path, 7 km, 3 hours.

outings.why: The round church at Østerlars, the smokehouse in Svaneke for a late lunch, the brewery, and the bus back with the bike; 28 km on quiet lanes and cycle paths, one real hill leaving Gudhjem.
outings.name: Gudhjem to Svaneke by bike via Østerlars
outings.season: April to October for bike hire
outings.fallback: Bus 3 to Svaneke for the smokehouse, 3 hours.

destination.name: Denmark
destination.pitch: Copenhagen is the reason people come and Jutland, Funen and the islands are the reason to stay a week: three nights in the capital, two in Aarhus, then either Skagen at the top of the country or Bornholm out in the Baltic, with Odense as th
destination.caveat: It is expensive in a way you cannot design around, roughly double Portugal for the same day, and outside June to August the light goes by four and half of Skagen and Bornholm is shuttered. Put together for you just now from a live search, so check anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.city: Copenhagen and Aarhus are real cities with real nights out, three hours apart by train.
because.food: Smørrebrød counters from 1877, the best bakeries in Europe, natural wine on every corner, smokehouses on Bornholm and more Michelin stars per head than anywhere north of Paris.
because.nature: Chalk cliffs at Møn, a migrating dune and two seas meeting at Skagen, granite coast on Bornholm; small, flat and reachable by train and bike, none of it wild.
because.culture: Louisiana, ARoS, Moesgaard and the Skagen painters, plus a design tradition you sleep in and sit on.
because.adventure: A cold swim, a cliff staircase and a boat to a fortress island are the limit; nothing here needs nerve.
because.relaxation: Harbour baths, saunas, beaches with no waves and a culture that closes the laptop at four; doing very little is the intended use.
because.exploration: Every town is walkable in an afternoon and the trains run on time, so a week can take in four bases without a car.
